title: Configuration, docs & deployment
purpose: The repo root is the configuration surface and documentation/deployment hub for the whole campus-helpdesk system. It holds the runtime config that the layered src/ stack consumes (config.yaml + .env templates read by src/campus_helpdesk/config/settings.py), the packaging and tooling metadata (pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, uv.lock), the human-readable documentation of the architecture and robot stack (README.md, CLAUDE.md, RASPBERRY_PI_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md, and the docs/ tree including service/interaction design docs and planning documents), and the Raspberry Pi deployment tooling (deployment/ with an apt/Ollama provisioning script and a systemd unit). It is the first place a developer or deployer interacts with the project, and it wires external services (Ollama, FAISS index location, embedding models, optional cloud LLM router) into the application through environment-derived Pydantic settings.

files.purpose: Primary runtime configuration for the src/campus_helpdesk stack, flattened into Pydantic Settings via a model_validator.

terms.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: the pipeline that retrieves relevant chunks (FAISS/BM25) and feeds them to a local LLM to answer campus questions.

An absolute score cutoff applied to hybrid-retriever distances before context building; here set to 999.0 to disable the broken absolute filter and rely on RRF ranking plus LLM grounding instead of rejecting valid FAISS-dominated results.
Cutoff below which retrieved evidence is considered too weak to ground an answer (0.75 here).
Score cutoff used by the answerability engine to decide whether the system can answer a query from the knowledge base at all (0.70 here).
Splitting source documents into overlapping chunks (chunk_size 800, chunk_overlap 120) before embedding and indexing.
A cross-encoder model (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) that re-scores the top candidate chunks after retrieval; top_n=20 candidates considered here.
The LLM KV-cache size in tokens; 2048 keeps RAM usage low on constrained machines.
Sampling parameters for the Ollama LLM that control token-selection diversity during generation.

files.notes: Loaded by settings.py via a model_validator(mode='before') that OVERWRITES same-named env vars, so config.yaml wins over .env for overlapping keys (e.g. retrieval.top_k -> RAG_SEARCH_LIMIT). Unknown keys ignored. The in-file comment documents that distance_threshold=2.0 previously caused hallucination; now 999.0 disables the filter. Note that ollama.model here is qwen2.5:3b while .env.example defaults to qwen2.5:7b, and temperature here is 0.0 vs 0.2 in .env.example.

terms.definition: A gitignored local file of KEY=VALUE settings loaded by pydantic-settings/dotenv; the application has no code default for the Ollama model name, so this file selects the model.

OFFLINE_LLM_MODEL names the local model used when the cloud generation router is disabled or unreachable (qwen2.5:3b here).

files.notes: Contains a placeholder OpenRouter API key (sk-or-v1-your-openrouter-api-key-here); a real key must never be committed here. data_flow: Configuration flows one way: root-level config.yaml and .env are consumed by src/campus_helpdesk/config/settings.py, which flattens config.yaml (nested app/retrieval/cache/memory/ollama/embedding/reranker/logging/vision/audio/vad/tts sections) via a model_validator and overlays env vars; config.yaml keys WIN over same-named env keys. The resulting Settings drive main.py -> OllamaLLMService -> create_rag_pipeline (hybrid retriever, FAISS store, reranker) -> RAGChatService, and also configure the robot-stack services (STT/TTS/VAD/vision). Packaging metadata in pyproject.toml defines the campus-helpdesk-ingest console entry point (campus_helpdesk.ingest:main) that builds the index, plus pytest/ruff/pyright config gating the verification flow (scripts/verify_project.py). Deployment flows outward to a Raspberry Pi: deployment/scripts/setup_pi_deployment.sh provisions the OS, installs Ollama + qwen2.5:3b, creates the venv from requirements.txt, pre-caches TTS, and installs the patched systemd unit deployment/systemd/campus-helpdesk-robot.service, which runs `python -m campus_helpdesk.robot_main` reading .env via EnvironmentFile. Documentation (README, CLAUDE.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, RASPBERRY_PI_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md, MODEL_SETUP.md, TROUBLESHOOTING.md, module-roadmap, planning docs, and service/interaction design docs) describes these same flows and is the reference consumed by humans during setup, tuning, and troubleshooting.

Raspberry Pi OS apt system packages: ffmpeg, espeak-ng, portaudio19-dev, libopenblas-dev, libatlas-base-dev, v4l-utils, cmake, build-essential
systemd (Linux init) for the campus-helpdesk-robot.service daemon
rhasspy/piper GitHub releases (standalone ARM64 Piper binary fallback, pinned 2023.11.14-2)
risks: config.yaml overrides same-named .env keys via the settings model_validator, so the two files can silently drift (CLAUDE.md calls this a known quirk); keep them in sync.

Default drift across sources: OLLAMA_MODEL qwen2.5:7b (.env.example) vs qwen2.5:3b (config.yaml, .env), temperature 0.2 vs 0.0, and RAG_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD 2.0 (.env.example, TROUBLESHOOTING.md) vs distance_threshold 999.0 (config.yaml) - the 2.0 value was removed because it caused hallucinations, so TROUBLESHOOTING.md is stale.
Two parallel dependency manifests (pyproject.toml/uv.lock vs requirements.txt) can drift; requirements.txt includes pyttsx3 not present in pyproject.toml.

Deployment docs reference scripts (scripts/semantic_chunker.py, build_embeddings.py, rebuild_faiss_store.py, download_piper_voices.py, voice_loop.py, precache_tts.py) that must exist; setup_pi_deployment.sh depends on scripts/precache_tts.py.
FAISS_ALLOW_DANGEROUS_DESERIALIZATION=true is enabled in the live .env and Pi guide (safe only for trusted, locally built indexes); the .env.example default is false.
.env.example ships a placeholder OpenRouter API key; a real key committed to the repo would be an exposure.
Legacy root config (config.py) duplicates settings.py values and is dead code not imported by src/ (per CLAUDE.md).

Docs describe features that are planning-only or dormant (analytics subsystem, KBMS incremental indexing, conversation manager, sentence-level validation engine); module-roadmap claims 550+ tests and Docker ARM64 containers that were not found in the repo.

setup_pi_deployment.sh's Piper ARM64 fallback is pinned to one release tarball (2023.11.14-2), a fragile external dependency; the primary pip install of piper-tts on ARM64 may fail and trigger the fallback.
The systemd unit is a template with /home/pi/campus-helpdesk and User=pi hardcoded; correct operation depends on setup_pi_deployment.sh's sed patching succeeding.

The repo root tracks large build artifacts (chunks.jsonl ~19MB, embedding_metadata.jsonl ~47MB, uv.lock ~254KB, many *_report.json files) inflating .git to ~900MB, partly negated by .gitignore rules that arrived after some files were committed.
README/DEPLOYMENT.md still reference legacy entrypoints (assistant_loop.py, demo.py, campus_helpdesk.scripts.ingest) and a stray D:\helpdesk\anti path, which can mislead new contributors.
